scope: research-reference-only; structural audit, no source video/frames in production cut list
centralQuestion: How should familiar control conventions reduce learning effort while preserving player customization, actual device capabilities and worthwhile distinctive controls?

lessonOrder.claim: Many first-person shooters share control conventions and a similar feel.
A shared input system can coexist with originality in immersion, world and story.
lessonOrder.visualRole: Presenter reasoning; convert to independent explanation, do not repeat as universal measured game claim.

lessonOrder.claim: Support genre newcomers; for players who already know a convention, established knowledge can reduce necessary explanation.
lessonOrder.visualRole: Known versus unfamiliar knowledge distinction, not a claim that all tutorials should be removed.

lessonOrder.claim: Familiar FPS action and weapon rules often need less detailed explanation; a contextual button prompt can be enough for a known action.
lessonOrder.visualRole: FPS gameplay montage, then Battlefield1 contextual melee prompt.
lessonOrder.caution: Reference narration usesR2/L1 as generic familiar-controller examples; do not assign these exact mappings to every shown game/platform.

lessonOrder.claim: Developers value originality, but practical de facto control standards can improve how people interact with games.
lessonOrder.visualRole: Canonical term: de facto standard / 사실상의 표준; use familiar-input transfer diagram.

lessonOrder.claim: Offer button remapping even when implementation is more complex.
lessonOrder.visualRole: Actual binding configuration screens, not generic fighting/racing action.

lessonOrder.claim: The designer’s preferred layout does not remove the value of player choice; allow adjustment where possible.
lessonOrder.visualRole: Designer declares ideal scheme while player wants a different one; independently create meaningful before/after UI.

lessonOrder.claim: Button reassignment cannot automatically preserve a feature that depends on analog input magnitude.
lessonOrder.visualRole: Switch Pro Controller Dpad highlighted, then Dpad0/1 versus variable analog-stick deflection.
lessonOrder.caution: Reference also notes sidewaysWiiRemote support inSuperSmashBrosBrawl existed but was less than ideal. Do not state everySmash title never allowed digital directional play or analog has literally infinite hardware precision.

lessonOrder.claim: Customization has functional limits; some required control behavior must remain or needs an actual redesign.
lessonOrder.visualRole: Return from exception to practical design tradeoff.

lessonOrder.claim: The closing aside illustrates an unexpectedly unfamiliar input mapping, followed by recognition that the input-to-action connection was wrong.
lessonOrder.visualRole: AtomicRunner gameplay then side-by-side correct/incorrect input mapping; the arcade story itself is the reference creator’s personal experience.
lessonOrder.caution: Do not present that arcade encounter as our experience, as Chelnov default controls, or Genesis footage as proof of arcade wiring. Preserve useful unfamiliar-mapping example with independently labeled hypothetical wiring diagram and ordinary licensed gameplay; personal biography can be omitted.

lessonOrder.claim: Learning an odd control scheme can itself be enjoyable; excessive standardization risks erasing distinctive kinds of play.
lessonOrder.visualRole: Concluding counterweight; not simply a checklist to standardize every control.
